evals.prompt: Search protocols.io for public CRISPR protocols and pull back the title and DOI for the top 10 results.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-protocolsio (or the connected protocols.io MCP tools). Calls GET https://www.protocols.io/api/v3/protocols with filter=public, key=CRISPR, and page_size=10 using the Bearer access token, checks the JSON status_code (0 = success), and prints each item's title and DOI (turning the dx.doi.org/ prefix into https://doi.org/).

assertions.value: Calls GET /protocols on the v3 API with a Bearer token and a keyword filter.

evals.prompt: Create a new protocol on protocols.io titled 'CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing Protocol', add its steps and materials, then publish it to get a DOI.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-protocolsio. Creates the protocol with POST /api/v3/protocols/<new GUID without dashes>, sets the title, description, and materials_text with PUT /api/v4/protocols/<guid>, adds steps with POST /api/v4/protocols/<guid>/steps chained by guid/previous_guid (first step previous_guid null), then issues the DOI with POST /api/v3/protocols/<uri>/publish (prepublish=1 to reserve the DOI without making it public), noting that publishing needs a title and an author and that a version with a DOI can no longer be edited.

assertions.value: Uses the v4 steps endpoint with guid/previous_guid ordering and the v3 publish endpoint; does not invent PATCH or /steps/reorder endpoints.

evals.prompt: Review the step-level comments on protocol 12345 on protocols.io and post a threaded reply answering a reviewer's question.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-protocolsio. Lists the comments with GET /api/v3/protocols/<protocol_uri>/comments, picks out step-level ones by their non-zero step_id and discussion_id, decodes the Draft.js comment body, and posts the threaded reply with POST /api/v3/steps/<step_id>/discussions/<discussion_id>/comments/<parent_id> (body plus protocol_uri).

evals.prompt: Upload my experimental results CSV into our protocols.io team workspace with tags so collaborators can find it.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-protocolsio. Uses the three-step upload: POST /api/v3/files with the filename to get S3 formData and a file_id, a multipart POST of the file to the returned S3 bucket, then PUT /api/v3/files/<file_id> to verify. Explains that the documented upload call has no workspace, folder, or tag fields, so the file is attached to a collection (collection_items, content_type_id 15) or organised in the web app.

assertions.value: Uses POST /v3/files, the S3 form upload, and PUT /v3/files/{file_id}; says tags are not part of the documented upload API instead of inventing a tags field.

evals.prompt: Create a Benchling ELN entry for today's run and link the DNA sequence entity I registered earlier into the entry notes.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-benchling. The user is working in Benchling's ELN/registry (entries.create_entry, inline entity links via the benchling-sdk), not authoring or publishing a protocols.io protocol.

evals.prompt: Back up my LabArchives notebook with all attachments and upload a PDF to one of its entries via the LabArchives REST API.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-labarchive. The platform is the LabArchives ELN (notebook backup, entry attachments), not protocols.io protocol management.

evals.prompt: Our methods paper is ready. Post the preprint to bioRxiv and get a DOI so we can cite it in the grant report.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-preprint-deposition. The user is depositing a manuscript preprint on bioRxiv, not publishing a protocol on protocols.io, even though both mint DOIs.
